# Evening two: the hop, the landing, and play

About 20 minutes.

1. **Draw drawings 7 to 12** from your chart, still two frames apart: drawing 7 on frame 13, drawing 9 (the top of the hop) on frame 17, and drawing 12, landing on the floor, on frame 23.
2. **Play it.** Watch it three times. Does it feel heavy? If it floats, your gaps near the floor are probably too small.
3. **Save a short video.** Film your screen with a phone while it plays, or save one from Blender (the steps are under "go deeper"). Either one counts.

→ [Blender manual: rendering an animation](asset:blender_viewport_render)

{{deeper}}

**Saving the video in Blender.** In Output Properties > Output, set Media Type to **Video**, and change the path box (it starts as /tmp/) to a folder you can find. Turn off the viewport's **Overlays** so the onion-skin ghosts are not saved. Then choose **View > Render Playblast**.

**Only 5 minutes?** Draw just drawings 9 and 12: the top of the hop and the landing.

**Having fun? Change what it is made of.** Keep the same 24 frames, and move the dots. A bowling ball barely hops at all. A rubber ball hops higher. What happens to the gaps?

**Look at your contact drawings one more time.** Does the ball really touch the floor on drawing 6, and on drawing 12? A hair of space under it is enough to make it float.
